findings.summary: Mon.id is an independent browser instance token, not native OT identity. Ordinary factory receives only OT text, not State or trainerId; capture only rewrites OT text.
Using Mon.id for shiny rejection falsely blocks the controlled ordinary starter. No native shiny classification is possible for arbitrary missing-OT legacy saves.

State.trainerId is a real separate profile field on newState and Egg gifts; old states may lack it and lazy Egg initialization can occur after ordinary acquisition, so later profile ID/name equality is not historical OT proof.

Ordinary createMon omits form. Native default CreateBoxMon starts from zeroed data; native form is a distinct5-bit field later modified by explicit callers. Fresh ordinary0 is source-supported, but missing old metadata is not raw-native proof.

proposal.freshForm: Store explicit form0 for ordinary source-backed default creations; caller-specific source form remains explicit for gifts/trainers/special encounters. Do not alter instance id or add RNG draws to obtain form.
proposal.freshOT: Thread a validated explicit known profile/preset OT identity from each actual source-owned creator/acquisition. Do not overload/rename/rewrite Mon.id or infer OT from name/current profile. Keep existing complete MonProvenance contract strict; use complete real origin context, or a separately typed narrow native-OT field/port if only OT is known, with explicit conflict validation instead of fake met/date/ball fields. A factory cannot discover an OT identity from its present text-only parameter.
proposal.oldArt: Explicit local-browser-v2 normal/base-art presentation compatibility when provenance is absent. No OT synthesized and no Mon/State writes in view. Valid present true OT uses native XOR and genuine shiny remains unsupported until real art; malformed present provenance must reject rather than fall through to legacy.
proposal.oldLogicalForm: Separate one-time explicit local-v2 base-form compatibility admission before queue/recovery; minimally admit old supported ordinary starter records as form0 with a compatibility receipt. Retain explicit nonzero/malformed/foreign forms as unsupported, never blanket queue-call default. This is browser policy, not recovery of native form. Do not synthesize OT as part of form policy.
proposal.queue: metadata.form stays required; current port may receive source-backed fresh form0 or an explicit legacy-adapter result. Current queue rejects ordinary nonzero transitions and must not guess.
